title: Manage by exception
blurb: Explain how tolerances on the seven aspects of performance delegate authority between levels, and when a problem must be escalated.
question: A stage is running 3% over budget, inside its 5% cost tolerance. The project manager wants to call an emergency board meeting. Is that consistent with manage by exception?

teach.body: Formally: a PRINCE2 project establishes limits of delegated authority by defining tolerances for performance against its plans. In plain English: each level of management is given room to manoeuvre. While things stay inside that room, they get on with it. Only when a deviation is forecast to go outside it do they pass the problem up to the level above.

teach.h: Tolerances cover seven aspects of performance
teach.caption: Sustainability is new in PRINCE2 7; older material lists only six tolerances.

teach.bottomLabel: Escalates upwards when a breach is forecast

teach.h: A forecast breach is an exception
teach.caption: Escalate when the FORECAST shows the line will cross tolerance, as early as possible, not after the money has gone.

teach.body: Manage by exception makes efficient use of senior management time: it reduces their burden without removing their control. Decisions are made at the right level, and the level above is alerted as early as possible when work will move outside tolerance. In people terms, decisions should sit at the most local level where the knowledge to make and own them resides; how much is delegated depends on confidence and trust, which can grow during the project.

root.label: A deviation appears in a stage

teach.caption: A forecast breach of PROJECT tolerance goes beyond the board to the business layer.

teach.h: The exception route for a stage

steps.label: Board decides
steps.sub: for example: exception plan, direction, close

teach.body: At Redbank County Libraries, the board gives project manager Femi Adebayo a stage tolerance of plus or minus two weeks and plus or minus 10% cost. Femi gives the joinery team manager, Kate Lowe, a work package tolerance of plus or minus three days. A late delivery costs Kate two days: she absorbs it. When a supplier failure is forecast to push the stage four weeks late, Femi raises an exception report straight away, before the stage actually overruns.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) An exception is a FORECAST breach, not only an actual one. (2) Setting tolerances is manage by exception, not manage by stages. (3) Scope tolerance (how far scope may vary) is manage by exception; defining the products in scope is focus on products. (4) Escalating a problem that is still within tolerance goes against the principle. (5) One detail from the risk practice: risk tolerance is set by the project board, based on the risk appetite the business determines (9.2.1).

items: Tolerances define limits of delegated authority for each level of plan.
Seven aspects: benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability, risk.
Business layer sets project tolerances; board sets stage tolerances; PM sets work package tolerances.
Escalate when a breach is forecast, as early as possible; otherwise manage within tolerance.
Saves senior management time without removing their control.

summary: You can now explain how manage by exception delegates authority through tolerances on seven aspects of performance, which level sets each tolerance and when an exception must be escalated. You can also tell it apart from manage by stages and focus on products.

A.q: Which statement describes the manage by exception principle?
options: Authority is delegated with tolerances against plans
The project is controlled through stage boundaries
Each problem is escalated to the board for decision
Lessons from exceptions are recorded for later use
A.why: A PRINCE2 project establishes limits of delegated authority by defining tolerances for performance against its plans (manual 2.5).

whyNot.1: Control through stage boundaries is manage by stages.
whyNot.2: Problems within tolerance are handled at the level that holds the tolerance.
whyNot.3: Recording lessons applies learn from experience.

A.q: Which of these is one of the seven aspects of performance against which tolerances are set?
options: Stakeholders
Communication
Sustainability
Resources
A.why: The seven are benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk. Sustainability is new in PRINCE2 7.

whyNot.0: Stakeholders are engaged through the people element, not set as a tolerance.
whyNot.1: Communication is managed through the communication management approach.
whyNot.3: Resources are planned, but resources is not one of the seven aspects.

A.q: Who sets the stage tolerances for a PRINCE2 project?
options: The business layer
The project manager
The team manager
The project board
A.why: The project board sets stage tolerances; the business layer sets project tolerances; the project manager sets work package tolerances.

whyNot.0: The business layer sets project-level tolerances.
whyNot.1: The project manager sets work package tolerances.
whyNot.2: The team manager works within work package tolerances.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. An exception is a situation where it can be [?] that there will be a deviation beyond the agreed tolerance levels.
options: confirmed
reported
forecast
assumed
B.why: An exception is based on a forecast: the deviation is predicted, so the next level can be alerted as early as possible.

whyNot.0: Waiting for confirmation would delay escalation; the trigger is a forecast.
whyNot.1: Reporting follows the forecast; it does not define the exception.
whyNot.3: An exception rests on a forecast from data and judgement, not an assumption.

B.q:
Which two statements about manage by exception are correct?
1. It reduces the burden on senior management without removing control.
2. Decisions should be made at the most local level that has the knowledge.
3. The project manager escalates every deviation from the stage plan.
4. Tolerances are set for cost and time but not for benefits.
options: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Manage by exception uses senior time efficiently without removing control (1), and decisions sit at the most local level where the knowledge resides (2).

whyNot.0: Statement 3 is false: deviations within tolerance are handled by the project manager.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: tolerances cover seven aspects, including benefits.
whyNot.3: Both are false: escalation is for forecast breaches, and benefits tolerances exist.

B.q: A stage is forecast to finish four days late. The stage time tolerance is plus or minus two weeks. What should the project manager do?
options: Raise an exception report to the project board
Ask the business layer for extra project time
Handle it within the stage without an exception
Close the stage early and request the next one
B.why: The forecast is within stage tolerance, so the project manager deals with it in controlling a stage; no exception report is needed.

whyNot.0: An exception report is for a forecast breach of stage tolerance, which has not happened.
whyNot.1: The business layer deals with project tolerance breaches.
whyNot.3: Ending a stage early is not a response to a deviation within tolerance.

C.q: A team manager forecasts that a work package will exceed its cost tolerance. To whom is this escalated, and how?
options: To the project board, as an exception report
To the project manager, as an issue
To the business layer, as a highlight report
To the executive, as a checkpoint report
C.why: Team managers escalate forecast work package breaches to the project manager as an issue; the PM handles work-package-level exceptions in controlling a stage.

whyNot.0: Team managers do not escalate to the board; only stage or project exceptions reach the board.
whyNot.2: Highlight reports go from the PM to the board, and a team manager does not escalate to the business layer.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports go to the project manager, not the executive.

C.q: Which tolerance is set by the business layer, and which level decides when it is forecast to be exceeded?
options: Stage tolerance; the project board
Project tolerance; the project board
Work package tolerance; the project manager
Project tolerance; the business layer
C.why: The business layer sets project tolerances and decides on forecast breaches of project tolerance.

whyNot.0: The board sets and decides on stage tolerances; the business layer sets project tolerances.
whyNot.1: The board cannot decide on a project tolerance breach; it goes to the business layer.
whyNot.2: The project manager sets work package tolerances, not the business layer.

C.q: How does manage by exception differ from focus on products when dealing with scope?
options: Exception sets how far scope may vary; products define what is in scope
Exception defines what is in scope; products set how far it may vary
Exception approves changes to scope; products record them in a register
Exception records scope in plans; products set scope in the business case
C.why: Scope tolerance (the permissible variation of a plan's products) is manage by exception; defining the products and their descriptions is focus on products.

whyNot.2: Approving changes is part of issue control; the difference is tolerance versus definition.
whyNot.3: Neither principle is defined by where scope is recorded.

reteach.title: A shopping trip with a budget
reteach.question: You send someone to buy supplies with £200 and say 'call me if it will be more than £220'. How does that match the principle?

blocks.body: Within £220 the shopper decides, without phoning you about every price. The moment they can see the total will go above £220, they phone, before paying, not after. That is manage by exception: a target, a tolerance, freedom inside it, and early escalation when a breach is forecast. PRINCE2 sets such limits for seven aspects (benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability, risk) at each level of plan.

blocks.text: Phone before the limit is crossed: an exception is a forecast, not an overspend that has already happened.

explain.body: A tolerance is the permissible deviation above and below a plan's target before escalation to the next level. Tolerances exist for seven aspects of performance.

test.q: What is a tolerance in PRINCE2?
options: A permissible deviation from a plan's target
The maximum budget approved for the project
A reserve held for approved changes to scope
The level of risk the business will accept
test.why: Tolerance is the permissible deviation above and below a plan's target before escalation.

whyNot.1: The approved budget is the target; tolerance is the room around it.
whyNot.2: A reserve for approved changes is the change budget.
whyNot.3: The business's attitude to risk is its risk appetite.

explain.body: Business layer sets project tolerances; the project board sets stage tolerances; the project manager sets work package tolerances; team managers work within them.

options: The project board
The team manager
The executive
The project manager
test.why: The project manager sets work package tolerances when authorizing work packages.

whyNot.0: The project board sets stage tolerances.
whyNot.1: The team manager works within work package tolerances.
whyNot.2: The executive, with the board, sets stage tolerances.

explain.body: An exception exists when a deviation beyond tolerance is forecast. The next level is alerted as early as possible, not after the breach.

test.q: When should the project manager raise an exception report?
options: When stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded
When a work package is a few days behind
When the stage has already overspent
When a risk is added to the risk register
test.why: The exception report is raised when a stage or project plan is forecast to exceed tolerance.

whyNot.1: A delay within tolerance is handled without escalation.
whyNot.2: Waiting for an actual overspend is too late; the trigger is a forecast.
whyNot.3: New risks are recorded and managed; they are not themselves exceptions.

explain.body: Senior managers are not involved in every decision, but they keep control because anything forecast to go outside their tolerances comes back to them.

test.q: What is a purpose of manage by exception?
options: To give the board day-to-day control
To remove the need for project reports
To use senior management time efficiently
To let team managers change stage plans
test.why: Manage by exception reduces the burden on senior management without removing their control.

whyNot.0: Day-to-day control is delegated to the project manager.
whyNot.1: Highlight and checkpoint reports are still produced.
whyNot.3: Stage plans are owned by the project manager and approved by the board.
